paper_sections.title: History of withdrawal modulates drug- and food-cue reactivity in cocaine dependent participants
Neural reactivity to DRUG and FOOD videos
Moderating role of drug use history and psychopathic traits

description.value: The study examined whether a history of DSM-assessed cocaine withdrawal modulates neural reactivity biases to drug- versus food-related reward cues, comparing cocaine-dependent participants with and without withdrawal and non-dependent controls, and exploring moderation by drug-use history and psychopathic traits.

design.value: Secondary analyses of an existing sample of 101 adult probation/parolees, divided into cocaine-dependent participants with lifetime withdrawal (WD; n = 20), cocaine-dependent participants without withdrawal (N-WD; n = 24), and non-dependent participants (ND; n = 57). Participants completed a cue-reactivity fMRI paradigm with two identical runs of drug- and food-related videos. Group, video type, and their interaction were tested using a mixed-model flexible-factorial analysis, followed by exploratory hierarchical regression analyses involving major drug use, psychopathic traits, and withdrawal group.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM Disorders (SCID-IV)

description.value: Administered by trained MA-level research staff to assess all psychiatric disorders, including the presence of lifetime cocaine dependence disorder.

Participants answered two questions about ever having withdrawal symptoms and using cocaine or another drug to prevent withdrawal symptoms, then confirmed dysphoric mood and at least two withdrawal symptoms within a few hours to several days following cessation of cocaine use.

A modified version was used to evaluate drug-use history and calculate a Major Drug Use (MDU) composite score by summating the number of years of regular use of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, and other amphetamine/opiates.
Used to collect more detailed information regarding participants’ cocaine use over the 90 days prior to the scanning session.
A semi-structured clinical assessment consisting of 20 items, each rated 0–2, with total scores ranging from 0 (low psychopathy) to 40 (high psychopathy).
Used to obtain full-scale IQ estimates; all participants scored >70 full-scale IQ.

task_description.value: Participants performed a cue-reactivity paradigm during which they viewed two identical runs of drug- and food-related videos.

stimuli.value: 29 videos (duration: ∼10,000–14,000 ms): 15 videos depicted individuals preparing or using cocaine, and 14 videos depicted individuals preparing or eating food. Videos were separated by an inter-trial jitter of either 2000, 3500, or 5000 ms.

description.value: Functional MRI was acquired while participants performed the cue-reactivity paradigm and viewed two identical runs of drug- and food-related videos.
fMRI data were previously preprocessed (realigned, normalized, smoothed) for the prior study.

model_settings.value: First-level analyses evaluated and compared the hemodynamic response during presentation of FOOD and DRUG videos. Six movement parameters (x,y,z, pitch, yaw, roll) were also included in the first-level design matrix.

The model included Group (WD, N-WD, ND), VideoType (DRUG, FOOD), and the Group*VideoType interaction. Whole-brain results were threshold at 0.001 uncorrected with an extended cluster threshold of 102 voxels (equivalent to p < .05 FWE). Small-volume corrected search spheres were 10 mm for cortical regions and 6 mm for subcortical regions.

Among dependent participants, Group (WD or N-WD), PCL-R scores and MDU scores were entered as separate first-level regressors, two-way interaction terms (Group * PCL-R, Group * MDU, PCL-R * MDU) were entered as second-level regressors, and the three-way interaction term was entered as a third-level regressor. Models were run both with and without age included in the model; reported results did not include age as a covariate.
